sentence: This project uses imaging to study how nitrous oxide changes neurons and their connections in animals, to explain its lasting effects on depressive symptoms.
This project tries to find out how a type of drug affects inflammation in women with angina and coronary microvascular disease.
This project studies how a lymphatic circuit in lymph nodes keeps cytotoxic T cells fighting tumors as melanoma spreads.
This project builds a microscope that gives sharp images across a wide range of light, from ultraviolet to infrared.
This project studies how the tick microbiome affects the way the Lyme spirochete spreads.
This project uses machine learning to measure and predict which antibiotic works well for urinary tract infections.
This project studies the role of growth plate stem cells in repairing the skeleton after injury.
This project studies how cancer starts, grows and spreads, and how anti-cancer treatments work.
This project builds measurements from images that predict whether oropharyngeal cancer will come back or spread to distant parts of the body.
This project tries to find out how antidepressants change the way the serotonin type 3 receptor works, at the level of molecules.
This project tests whether e-health prevention strategies can work together to reduce sexual violence and alcohol misuse on college campuses.
This project tries to find out which gene variants are linked to compulsive alcohol use in genetically diverse rats.
This project builds a resource that offers nonhuman primate models and tools for testing gene therapy, genome editing and regenerative medicine.
This project builds a dual-energy CT method that measures what tissue is made of during molecular imaging.
This project studies how fibro/adipogenic progenitors and their metabolism lead to muscle fibrosis and sarcopenia with age.
This project studies how circadian clocks in mammal tissues respond directly to short-wavelength light using opsin photoreceptors.
This project studies how photoreceptors respond to hyperglycemia and add to inflammation in the retina in diabetic retinopathy.
This project studies how cholangiocarcinoma switches between lineage states and how this affects tumor growth and drug resistance, using mouse models.
This project builds an analytic tool that recognizes what toddlers are doing, such as walking, standing or sitting, to measure physical activity.
This project tests whether tirzepatide changes colorectal cancer incidence and outcomes in a genetically engineered mouse model.
